title: Cheese and Garlic Crack Bread (Pull Apart Bread)
description: This is garlic bread - on crack! Great to share with a crowd, or as a center piece for dinner accompanied by a simple salad. The denser the bread, the better the pieces will hold together when pulled off. Sourdough works best. When it comes out of the oven, it’s all golden, crusty and buttery on the inside and you know that’s just the start of the eating experience that’s about to commence…then the devouring begins…. that cheesy pull! That buttery, garlicky bread!! And yet, and yet, there’s even more to come…everybody goes so nuts over the cheese bits that you pull out, but my favorite part is the base of the bread. All the butter and cheese drips to the bottom and it bakes so nice and crisp.
ingredients: 1 cup shredded Mozzarella cheese (or other melting cheese)
100 g / 1 stick (8 tbsp) unsalted butter , softened
directions: Combine butter, garlic and salt in a heatproof bowl and melt in the microwave. Stir in the parsley.
Cut the bread on a diagonal into 2cm/1" diamonds but do not cut all the way through the bread.

Use your fingers or a knife to pry open each crack and drizzle in a teaspoon of butter and stuff in a pinch of cheese. This might sound like a bit of an effort, but I promise you it is worth it! You don't need to be super neat, it's nice to have some of the butter drizzled over the crust.
Wrap with foil and bake for 20 minutes until the cheese has mostly melted, then unwrap and bake for 5 - 10 minutes more to make the bread nice and crusty.

Make Ahead - The best way to make ahead is to use softened butter instead of melted butter, mix with garlic, salt, and parsley then smear into the cracks. Stuff with cheese, wrap and refrigerate or freeze. To cook, thaw then follow recipe instructions to bake.
